techPlan.problem: Chinese chess progress can still be blocked by missing temporal signals, concurrent UI updates, or untracked schema changes.
invariants: Every completed move must commit turn, board, phase, clock, repetition, and schema revision as one immutable state snapshot.
User, AI, and control actions must use a monotonic action id so a late asynchronous result cannot move the next turn.
Draw and forced-win thresholds must read engine-approved evidence, not arbitrary browser behavior.
Shared board, history, and memory snapshots must remain immutable.
Persistence upgrades must either complete as one transaction or provide an atomic rollback path.
Restart must restore the snapshot and then prove a legal next move before accepting input.
verification: Run the AI-versus-AI migration checker until a terminal state or an explicit bounded draw test is reached.
Add focused tests before updating rules, persistence, clocks, or snapshot helpers.

migrationPlan.unknownState: Treat absent positionHistory and repetition counters as new-game defaults, not undefined bugs.
nextRevision: Record repetition and draw evidence in the state snapshot.
Then expose the result through getGameStatus.
Then render and verify the result in the browser.

inboxUpload.rule: Keep one definitive example artifact; do not maintain unverified model-copy variants.
inboxUpload.evidence: Current AI code lives in examples/chinese-chess/ai.js and has node --test evidence.

history.summary: Added AI and temporal rules to the skill, a 20-turn no-repeat test, and a template-based AI progress simulation.
Added temporal migration checks across AI and game state, plus the fail-hard suggestion skill artifacts.
